content.text:
I have what I need. Let me confirm my analysis of the termination architecture:

**Findings:**
- **Term structure:** 1-year Initial Term, auto-renewing in 1-year increments (p0016) — no multi-year committed term.
- **Customer convenience right:** Exists — "for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice." Sits at the top of the fallback band (60–90 days).
- **Vendor convenience right:** Same 90 days' notice — at, not below, the 90-day walk-away floor.
- **Early-termination cost:** No penalty or ETF; Kubient only takes "fees generated during the termination period" (the 90-day notice window) — i.e. revenue share on impressions actually served, within the fallback's 3-months cap.
- **Prepaid-fee refund:** Not applicable — §5 (p0023) is a pure revenue-share with sequential-liability payment flow, so there are no prepaid fees to refund.

This meets the fallback on every material term, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale:
Paragraph 4(a) sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore acceptable without redline. (1) We hold a convenience right: either Party may terminate "for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice," which is within the fallback's 60–90 day band. (2) The Initial Term is only one (1) year, auto-renewing in 1-year increments, so the convenience lock-out applies to a term of exactly 12 months and does not trigger the detection test for "a term longer than 12 months" — we are not trapped in a multi-year commitment (walk-away territory). (3) There is no early-termination fee or penalty: Kubient is entitled only to "all fees generated during the termination period," i.e. revenue share on impressions actually served during the 90-day notice window, which is at or below the fallback's 3-months'-fees cap and is compensation for services rendered rather than a punitive exit charge. (4) The Vendor's reciprocal convenience right is at 90 days' notice, which meets the fallback floor; walk-away is only triggered by Vendor convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred position but are noted rather than flagged: the notice period is 90 days rather than 30, and the Vendor's convenience right is exercisable at any time after the Initial Term rather than strictly at the end of a renewal term. Neither is material here given the short 1-year cycle and the reciprocity of the notice period. The absence of a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund is moot: §5 (p0023) is a pure revenue-share under which Kubient collects from Advertisers and remits to Customer within seven days of receipt, so Customer pays no fees in advance and has nothing to reclaim.
